rubrics.criterion: Receive-side consumption accounting for a stream — advancing the cumulative read counter and unread increment plus deciding when a consumed-bytes announcement is due — is decided by stream-side code working on its own state, at both the direct-read site (in the v2 read path) and the ReadTo-style accounting site.
rubrics.rationale: This counter mutation and trigger decision is the primary piece of stream bookkeeping the injected session surface moved off the stream; a solver that leaves it on the session has not resolved the instance.

rubrics.criterion: The v2 send-window computation that gates stream writes — in-flight bytes as written minus peer-consumed, subtracted from the peer-advertised window — is performed by stream-side code on its own window state, with the current maths preserved including the early-return behavior for negative in-flight values.
rubrics.rationale: The write path's window gate is the second hot-path relocation in this instance; its three window counters live on the stream, so the calculation must be requested from the stream side.

rubrics.criterion: The buffered-payload volume of a stream's receive storage is computed through the ring's own side (or an equivalent owner-side seam), so the slot/index/mask/head layout of the receive ring is no longer walked by a method whose receiver is not that storage.
rubrics.rationale: The ring's layout details are private to the ring; any repair that keeps the scan reachable from the session-facing surface leaves the ring exposed across its ownership boundary.

rubrics.criterion: The per-stream snapshot construction — identity, cumulative counters, in-flight and peer-window values, buffered volume, and the read-closed/write-closed/closed flags — is assembled by the stream itself, while the session-side entry point still resolves a stream id through the session's stream table and preserves the not-found behavior for unknown or already-removed stream ids.
rubrics.rationale: Only the registry lookup is genuinely the session's responsibility in this surface; the data assembly belongs to the stream that owns every sampled field.

rubrics.criterion: The queued-frames and queued-payload-bytes aggregation for the write scheduler is computed by the scheduler queue itself under its own synchronization discipline, and session-side code no longer reads the queue's pending counter, round-robin list or per-stream heap table directly.
rubrics.rationale: The scheduler's internal container topology is used by this aggregation; keeping the walk outside the queue leaves the session coupled to scheduling-queue internals.

rubrics.criterion: The session-facing introspection surface keeps operating with unchanged exported names, signatures and observable semantics: the per-stream accounting lookup callable by stream id with its found flag, and the scheduler backlog pair, both remaining non-blocking samples of live state.
rubrics.rationale: The introspection surface is the reason this maintenance work exists; deleting or reshaping it must not be a path to satisfaction, and its sampling semantics are the observable contract.

rubrics.criterion: All three production call sites that were rewired onto session-level mediation — the v2 direct-read accounting, the ReadTo-style accounting, and the v2 write-path window gate — now call their owner-side equivalents directly, with no call path still handing a stream to a session method so the session can compute on it.
rubrics.rationale: The instance is incomplete if only the construction sites move and the hot-path callers keep the stream-through-session detour, since the mediation pattern survives at every unrepaired call site.

rubrics.criterion: Concurrency discipline carries across the relocation: consumption counters keep being mutated under the same stream buffer discipline the accounting call sites already apply, and window arithmetic keeps using atomic loads for the written, consumed and advertised counters it samples.
rubrics.rationale: These counters cross goroutine boundaries in the live transport; a relocation that drops the existing serialization or atomicity silently trades a design fix for a data race.

rubrics.criterion: No exported construct of the pinned revision loses its name, signature or meaning as a side effect of the move (the exported stream wrapper keeps its behavior, and any internal relocation stays invisible in the package's existing exported surface).
rubrics.rationale: This is an internal ownership re-balancing inside one package; breaking the existing public API would change a compatibility boundary the task explicitly holds stable.

rubrics.criterion: Relocated aggregation stays lock-light and consistent with the existing lock order: if the scheduler backlog takes the queue's mutex, it does not acquire other locks or perform blocking channel operations while holding it, and no other relocated site introduces a new cross-component lock nesting.
rubrics.rationale: Diagnostics must remain safe to call while the transport and scheduler loops run; a repair that restores ownership but introduces an lock cycle or unbounded blocking still regresses the live path.

rubrics.criterion: The session-level helper methods that take a stream as an operand are gone entirely — declarations and bodies removed — rather than surviving alongside the new owner-side seams.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the operand-taking session helpers in the tree keeps the very mediation shape this task asks to remove, and dangling bodies invite future callers to reuse the misplaced path.

rubrics.criterion: No dead or bypassed copy of the relocated logic stays behind: no unused method, unreached branch or orphaned body duplicating the consumption, window, scanning or aggregation behavior remains once the owner-side seams are in place.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that adds owner-side implementations without removing what they replace leaves two competing definitions of stream accounting in one package, inviting divergence on the next edit.

rubrics.criterion: Vestigial consequences of the move are cleaned up: imports that only served the removed session-side code are dropped, and no doc comments or field notes keep directing readers to the removed session-level helpers.
rubrics.rationale: Stale references to the removed seams misdirect the next maintainer exactly where the ownership boundary was supposed to become clear, undercutting the reason for the move.

rubrics.criterion: Consumed-bytes announcements are emitted on a different rule than before: they stop firing on a stream's first read or on the accumulated-increment threshold, fire on every read, never fire, or double-announce the same consumption, changing flow-control for the peer.
rubrics.rationale: The announcement trigger is subtle read-path state machine whose exact rule (first read plus accumulated threshold) is easy to disturb while relocating the counters.

rubrics.criterion: Malformed peer accounting gets silently absorbed during the move: negative in-flight accounting is clamped to zero, retried, or treated as valid, instead of surfacing the same distinct write error the v2 write path returns today.
rubrics.rationale: The early-return guard exists to reject a hostile or broken peer claiming more consumption than bytes sent; flattening it away converts a protocol check into silent mis-writing.

rubrics.criterion: Consumption counters mutate outside the buffer discipline the accounting call sites previously held: the sequence advancing the read counter and increment, testing the threshold and resetting the increment is no longer serialized with the ring operations it mirrors.
rubrics.rationale: The paired update-and-reset sequence only stays consistent because both accounting sites hold the stream's buffer discipline; moving any step outside it re-opens interleavings that reset or report torn counters.

rubrics.criterion: The introspection surface blocks or deadlocks the live transport: sampling now waits on transport channels, or a relocated aggregate holds the scheduler queue's mutex while acquiring another lock, freezing the send, receive or scheduler loops.
rubrics.rationale: The snapshot and backlog are sampled by operators while the connection is busy; converting a non-blocking sample into a lock-order participant is the most plausible silent regression a relocation can introduce.

rubrics.criterion: The non-v2 stream paths change behavior as a side effect: version-1 reads start emitting consumed announcements or alter token-return behavior, or version-2-only state starts being consumed by version-1 accounting.
rubrics.rationale: The relocated logic sits near version-specific branches; a solver that generalizes the accounting across protocol versions would silently change the v1 wire behavior the tests hold fixed.
